expected_signature: 12 byte binary number exceeds maximum signed long value
ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each byte position of the field together with the bit position of the value that belongs there; hops 1 and 2 decide the form (octal limit per field length, negative values binary) and reject values too large for fields shorter than nine bytes, hop 3 passes the field along and hop 4 returns the offset after it. Once the field is written, no caller can tell which leading bytes repeat low bytes of the value and which carry its sign without recomputing the field. The convention is pinned outside the gold: TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary reads a field of nine or more bytes as a signed big-endian number (parseBinaryBigInteger builds a BigInteger from the bytes after the marker), so the leading bytes of a 12-byte field must carry the sign; TarUtils.formatBigIntegerBinary fills the bytes between the marker and the value's own bytes with 0xff for a negative value; TarUtilsTest testReadNegativeBinary12Byte reads -3601 from ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff f1 ef, and testOldEntryStarMode expects a negative 12-byte modification time to start with 0xff. The gold's javadoc promises that the remaining bytes hold the number, which the 12-byte field written for 0xff00000000000001 does not.
